event_confirmation: Company press release dated 2026-10-13 (ir.blackriflecoffee.com detail/118): 'will release the third quarter 2026 financial results on Monday, November 2, 2026, after market close', call Tuesday November 3, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The sweep's 'Q3 2025 was Nov 4' was the call date; the Q3 2025 release was Nov 3 amc, the same Monday-amc / Tuesday-call pattern.
conviction_note: The bar is the company's own Q3 guide (revenue at least +5%, about $106M; adj. EBITDA about $7M; GM approaching 36%) and the street sits on it; BRCC has beaten consensus three quarters running, and the FY floor (about $430M) leaves H2 flat y/y after H1 +17%, so a beat and a mechanical guide raise are plausible (print_vs_bar +2%). But the stock is +33% in 20 sessions with no identified catalyst, five of its last seven prints fell, and the Q2 beat-and-affirm traded 0.0%. So the findings sum to a small positive (+0.6) and p_up sits at 51 on a 13-point absolute move.
bar: Company guide for Q3 2026 given on the 2026-08-04 call: revenue growth 'at least 5%, or roughly $106M', adj. EBITDA 'approximately $7 million', gross margin to 'approach 36%' (https://www.webull.com/news/15344801058595840). Estimates agree: Yahoo 3 analysts avg $105.89M (range $104.87-106.5M), Benzinga Q3'26E $105.9M, EPS $0.01 (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BRCC/analysis/, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BRCC/earnings-forecasts). FY2026 guide affirmed 2026-08-03: revenue at least +8% (about $430M), adj. EBITDA at least +35% (about $29M), GM 34-36%.
positioning_check: Short interest 475K shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, 5.2 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/brcc). The 2026-09-30 settlement was 448.5K and 3.8 DTC. Against about 12M post-split Class A shares (119.8M before the 1:10 split per the Q2 10-Q) that is about 4% of Class A: not crowded. No usable option chain: ATM spread is 158% of mid, so there is no skew. Put/call OI is 6.0, but total OI is only 770. Tape: +7.98% over 5 days, +33.1% over 20 days, +39% over the month; spot $12.58 is 29% below the 52-week high ($17.80 on 2026-05-21) and 101% above the low ($8.04 on 2026-08-31). Avg volume is 119K shares, about $1.5M a day. Founder Evan Hafer is selling about 12K shares a day under a 10b5-1 plan.

findings.finding: Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to 'at least 5%, or roughly $106M' (about flat with Q2's $107.0M), adj. EBITDA to about $7M and GM to approach 36%. Consensus ($105.9M, 3 analysts) sits exactly on that guide. BRCC beat consensus in each of the last three quarters (Q2: $107.0M vs a $103.7M estimate, +3.2%), and management says the guide counts only 'confirmed commercial drivers', so a modest beat of the company's own number is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-03): revenue +3.2% over consensus, guide only affirmed, stock 0.0% ($10.50 to $10.50), then -18% by 2026-08-10. Q1 2026 (2026-05-04): revenue +21.4% with a raise, +23.85%. Five of the seven baseline reactions were negative.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide and consensus are public, so the bar itself is priced. What is not priced is whether the company clears its own conservative number by the Q2 margin (3%). A beat of that size is inside normal noise and the Q2 version bought 0.0%. That is why this is small.
findings.independence: The Benzinga earnings table shows beats in each of the last three quarters (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BRCC/earnings-forecasts). It shares the beat-history fact with nothing else in this file.

findings.finding: The affirmed FY2026 floor (revenue at least +8%, about $430.2M on FY2025's $398.3M) less H1 2026 actuals ($109.2M + $107.0M = $216.2M) needs only $214.0M in H2, against $213.4M in H2 2025 ($100.7M + $112.7M), so H2 growth of +0.3% after H1 +17%. The EBITDA floor ($28.9M less H1 $13.6M = $15.3M) is below H2 2025's $18.1M. A Q3 near $108M leaves room to raise the FY floor mechanically. Management explained the deceleration: pricing benefit moderating from Q3, about $5M of non-recurring liquidation revenue in Q4 2025, fuel-price pressure on convenience/RTD, and $5-6M of extra H2 marketing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A raise in Q1 2026 (revenue to at least +8% from +7%, EBITDA to at least +35% from +30%) bought +23.85%. An affirm in Q2 2026 bought 0.0%. Guidance direction has been the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but nobody aggregates it. The street's Q4 estimate ($110.1M, Benzinga) is still below Q4 2025's $112.7M, so consensus models the guide floor rather than a raise. If a raise were priced, Q4 estimates would sit above the prior year. Against this: the +33% 20-day run-up may already carry raise expectations (see the run-up finding).
findings.independence: Q4 2025 and FY2025 figures come from the 2026-03-02 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260302231224/en/brc-inc.-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results/). Q1 2026 comes from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001891101/000189110126000027/brcinc_exhibit991xq1fy2026.htm. The management cadence commentary comes from the same call transcript as the first finding.

findings.finding: BRCC closed at $8.94 on 2026-10-01 and $12.60 on 2026-10-30 (+33% over 20 sessions, +39% over the month) on rising volume (Oct 27-29: 175-189K vs a 119K average). I found no company news, upgrade or dated catalyst for the run other than the 2026-10-13 date notice. The name goes into the print with a large unexplained run-up after five down reactions in its last seven prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the +23.85% Q1 reaction the stock peaked at $17.80 on 2026-05-21 and then gave back more than half by August. 2025 prints fell -7.0%, -15.8%, -25.7% and -16.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is filed as the expectation the print has to beat: a run of this size with no identified cause means a merely in-line beat-and-raise may already be paid for. If the market had no raise in the price, the stock would still sit near the $9-10 post-Q2 range.
findings.independence: The founder's 10b5-1 selling into the run (next finding) is a different source pointing to supply into strength. No source explains the run itself.

findings.finding: Founder, director and 10% owner Evan Hafer (via EKNRH Holdings) sold 12,000 shares on each of 2026-10-27 ($11.37) and 2026-10-28 ($11.78) under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-06-15. A Form 144 filed 2026-10-19 covers 96,000 Class A shares (about $1.0M). Further Form 4s were filed on 10-15 and 10-20. This is steady scheduled supply of about 10% of average daily volume into a thin name.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none specific; the founder also sold 2,000,000 pre-split shares at $1.49 (Form 4 filed 2026-06-03) ahead of a stock that later fell to its low.
findings.why_not_priced: The sales are filed but small and pre-planned (10b5-1), so they carry little information about the quarter. The only effect is mechanical supply. If the market treated it as informed selling, the run-up would have stalled on the Form 144.
findings.independence: The Form 144 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1891101/000197407826000383/primary_doc.xml, 2026-10-19) is the same seller.

findings.finding: US gasoline was at record prices in September 2026 and it weighed on gas-station and c-store impulse traffic (Placer.ai September index; retail sales +0.8% in September, driven almost entirely by gasoline). BRCC's RTD business runs through convenience: RTD ACV fell to 52.4% from 53.4% in Q2, and management already cited 'higher fuel prices affecting channel traffic' when it set the Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none; RTD has not been the line BRCC traded on in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission and mostly inside the guide: management named fuel prices when it set Q3 at about $106M. The incremental part is that prices went higher still into September. Wholesale packaged coffee (grocery/mass, the larger line) is not hit the same way. Net of the rest of the company, this is small.
findings.independence: AP retail sales story, 2026-10-15 (https://www.ksat.com/business/2026/10/15/retail-sales-up-08-in-september-but-a-big-chunk-of-spending-went-to-paying-gasoline-bills/). This is a proxy; neither the company nor a counterparty has confirmed it for Q3.

findings.finding: Green coffee for 2026 is locked at $2.95/lb, so the guided Q3/Q4 GM of about 36% is largely determined. About 50% of 2027 needs is covered at $2.65/lb, versus arabica futures near $2.95/lb on 2026-10-02 and about $3.10 on 10-20. A blended 2027 cost of about $2.80-2.85 is roughly 3-5% below 2026. That supports any first 2027 margin commentary on the call, though the uncovered half is exposed to renewed volatility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin was the 2025 line: GM declines of 520bp in Q3 2025 and 600bp in Q4 2025 accompanied the -7.0% reaction and the start-of-2026 lows.
findings.why_not_priced: The 2027 cover was disclosed on the call, but no 2027 estimate visible in aggregators reflects it. The market will only react if management frames 2027 on the Q3 call, which is not certain (2026 was guided in March).
findings.independence: Arabica futures level: https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/coffee/news/589148 (about 2026-10-02). It shares the call transcript with the first two findings.

findings.finding: J.M. Smucker booked about $115M of IEEPA tariff refunds in its quarter to 2026-07-31, which boosted US coffee segment profit 124% (IEEPA tariffs were invalidated by the Supreme Court on 2026-02-20; CBP's CAPE refund process has run since 2026-04-20). BRCC's Q2 10-Q cites tariffs as a COGS headwind but discloses no refund receivable. If BRCC was importer of record on 2025 green coffee, a refund could land in Q3 COGS. It is unknown whether BRCC imported directly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none at BRCC. Across the repo's resolved days a tariff refund landing moved stocks in the direction of guidance, not the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing in BRCC's filings or consensus ($0.01 EPS, about $7M EBITDA guide) reflects a refund. If one were expected, the EBITDA estimate would sit above the company's $7M guide. As a one-off with no stated path to the guide, it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: The BRCC Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1891101/000189110126000039/brrc-20260630.htm) confirms tariffs were paid as a cost and that no refund is recorded. Background on refund eligibility: https://www.americanactionforum.org/shipment/pointless-coffee-tariffs/

rejected_candidates.candidate: Smucker US Retail Coffee net sales +13% (pricing and volume at Dunkin'/Bustelo) in the quarter to 2026-07-31, as a read on packaged coffee category health
rejected_candidates.detail: The category trend is already in BRCC's own company-cited Nielsen data and Q3 guide; the Smucker document is used once, in the tariff-refund finding.

rejected_candidates.candidate: KDP H1 2026 US Coffee volume -9.7% on price elasticity and single-serve softness, as a negative pod read-across
rejected_candidates.detail: Covers a period BRCC already reported. BRCC's own Q2 Nielsen (+28.2% vs category +9.9%) and its pod share gains contradict transmission to BRCC; a judge may disagree.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew. The +33% 20-day run-up cuts against the positive guidance arithmetic, since a beat-and-raise may already be in the price. Together with the name's habit of selling prints (5 of 7 down, Q2 beat flat), that holds p_up near 50 despite a fundamental read that leans to a beat.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; the Q2 beat traded 0.0%): the reported-quarter beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5.
Lesson 5 (an unexplained move in a microcap is worth little): the run-up/positioning finding cut from -1.5 to -0.8, kept because the run-up sets the bar the print must clear.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the tariff refund cut from +0.3 to +0.2, lands_on one_off, no path to the guide.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so no cap. Lesson 7: short interest checked, about 4% of Class A and 5.2 DTC, not crowded. Lesson 8 does not apply (no confirmed unpriced company number). Guidance finding left at +1.0; abs_move raised from 12 to 13 for thin turnover and a possible guide change.
